title: Tool Selection Quality Score Alert
dataSources: Tool Selection Quality scores on sampled traces, aggregated by the stream alert
description: Notifies the prompt owner when the average Tool Selection Quality score on an Agent Stream falls below the agreed level, using an evaluator alert on the stream's Alerts tab.
value: A deploy that confuses the agent's tool choice shows first as falling scores. An alert turns that trend into a notification while the change is still easy to roll back.
implementation: On the Agent Stream's Alerts tab, add an alert on the Tool Selection Quality evaluator with aggregation average, a threshold from the stream's normal score, and a window. Route it to the prompt owner.
visualization: Alerts tab history; Tool Selection Quality over time.
knownFalsePositives: An alert on an evaluator only sees sampled traces; at a low sample rate a few wrong scores move the average a lot. Raise the sample rate or lengthen the window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open the Agent Stream, go to the Alerts tab and add an alert. Each alert is an evaluator or a built-in metric (Status Code, Cost, Latency, Trace Count), an aggregation (average, min, max, count or sum), a threshold and a window. Notifications go to email, a Slack incoming webhook or a generic HTTP webhook. Alerts never block a request. Any evaluator enabled on the stream can be added. A generic HTTP webhook receives a body with `event` (`alert.triggered`), `conditions[].observed_value`, `dedup_key`, `deep_link` and any `metadata` configured on the webhook. Webhook auth is none, bearer or HTTP basic, and the credential is write-only after save.

Step 3 — Validate

Confirm the evaluator is enabled (`get_metrics()`), then trigger the alert on a test stream with a high threshold. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Link the alert to the release process so a firing alert prompts a rollback review.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Alert never fires: the evaluator is missing from the stream's set (UC-13.8.22) or no traces were sampled in the window.
grandmaExplanation: We get a message when the reviewer starts seeing the assistant pick the wrong tools more often than usual.

productArtifacts.title: Tool Selection Quality alert
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Alerts tab > add alert
Metric: Tool Selection Quality (evaluator enabled on the stream)
Aggregation: average
Condition: Average score below the agreed level for the window
Window: match the team's response time; a shorter window alerts sooner and is noisier
Notification: email, Slack incoming webhook, or generic HTTP webhook
Notes: Only sampled traces are counted.
